title: Acts Chapter 8 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Acts chapter 8 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Acts Chapter 8 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Acts Chapter 8.

questions.question: In Acts 8, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The apostles sending Peter and John to Samaria
questions.correctAnswer: Saul consenting unto Stephen's death
questions.explanation: Acts 8:1 states that Saul was consenting unto Stephen's death at the start of the chapter, which is the earliest event mentioned.

questions.question: Who carried Stephen to his burial according to Acts 8?
questions.correctAnswer: Devout men
questions.explanation: Acts 8:2 states that devout men carried Stephen to his burial.

questions.question: What did Saul do to the church before his conversion?
options: Made havoc of the church, entering into every house
Sent Peter and John to Samaria
questions.correctAnswer: Made havoc of the church, entering into every house
questions.explanation: Acts 8:3 tells us Saul made havoc of the church, entering into every house and haling men and women to prison.

questions.question: What did those scattered abroad do after the persecution?
questions.correctAnswer: Went everywhere preaching the word
questions.explanation: Acts 8:4 says those that were scattered abroad went everywhere preaching the word.

questions.question: To which city did Philip go to preach Christ?
questions.correctAnswer: Samaria
questions.explanation: Acts 8:5 states that Philip went down to the city of Samaria to preach Christ.

questions.question: How did the people respond to Philip's preaching?
options: With one accord they gave heed
They reported him to the authorities
questions.correctAnswer: With one accord they gave heed
questions.explanation: Acts 8:6 indicates the people with one accord gave heed to Philip's words.

questions.question: What miracles did Philip perform in Samaria?
options: Unclean spirits came out, and many palsies and lame were healed
questions.correctAnswer: Unclean spirits came out, and many palsies and lame were healed
questions.explanation: Acts 8:7 describes unclean spirits coming out with a loud voice and many palsies and lame being healed by Philip.

questions.question: What was the reaction in the city after Philip's miracles?
questions.correctAnswer: There was great joy
questions.explanation: Acts 8:8 states that there was great joy in that city after the miracles.

questions.question: Who was Simon, mentioned in Acts 8?
options: A man who used sorcery and bewitched the people of Samaria
A devout man who buried Stephen
questions.correctAnswer: A man who used sorcery and bewitched the people of Samaria
questions.explanation: Acts 8:9 introduces Simon as a man who used sorcery and bewitched the people of Samaria.

questions.question: What did the people say about Simon before his belief?
options: This man is the great power of God
He is a servant of Philip
questions.correctAnswer: This man is the great power of God
questions.explanation: Acts 8:10 records the people saying Simon was the great power of God.

questions.question: What happened when people believed Philip's preaching about the kingdom of God?
options: They were baptized, both men and women
questions.correctAnswer: They were baptized, both men and women
questions.explanation: Acts 8:12 says that when they believed Philip's preaching, they were baptized, both men and women.

questions.question: Simon himself believed and was baptized. What did he do afterwards?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Acts 8:13 states Simon believed, was baptized, and continued with Philip, wondering at the miracles and signs.

questions.question: The apostles at Jerusalem sent Peter and John to Samaria after hearing the word had been received there.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Acts 8:14 confirms the apostles at Jerusalem sent Peter and John to Samaria after hearing the word of God was received.

questions.question: Saul was the one who baptized the new believers in Samaria.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text does not say Saul baptized anyone; rather, Philip preached and baptized in Samaria (Acts 8:5, 12-13).

questions.question: The people of Samaria immediately rejected Philip's message because he was from Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Acts 8:6 shows the people gave heed with one accord to Philip's message; they did not reject it.

medium.title: Acts Chapter 8 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Acts Chapter 8 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who prayed for the new believers that they might receive the Holy Ghost?
questions.correctAnswer: Peter and John
questions.explanation: Acts 8:15 states that Peter and John prayed for them so that they might receive the Holy Ghost.

questions.question: What does Acts 8:22 promise will happen if someone repents of their wickedness and prays to God?
questions.correctAnswer: They will be forgiven
questions.explanation: Acts 8:22 commands repentance and prayer to God, and Acts 8:24 shows Simon asking for prayer so that these things do not come upon him, implying forgiveness is promised upon genuine repentance.

questions.question: What was Simon's reaction when he saw the apostles laying hands and giving the Holy Ghost?
options: He offered them money to receive the same power
He challenged them to a miracle contest
questions.correctAnswer: He offered them money to receive the same power
questions.explanation: Acts 8:18 records Simon offering money to the apostles to receive the power of giving the Holy Ghost.

questions.question: How does Peter respond to Simon's offer of money, and what reason does he give?
options: Peter accepts the money but warns Simon
Peter rebukes Simon saying the gift of God cannot be bought
Peter asks Simon to pray for the apostles
questions.correctAnswer: Peter rebukes Simon saying the gift of God cannot be bought
questions.explanation: Acts 8:20 shows Peter saying 'Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money.'

questions.question: What practical lesson about integrity can be learned from Peter's rebuke of Simon?
options: Spiritual gifts cannot be earned or bought
Money can buy influence in the church
questions.correctAnswer: Spiritual gifts cannot be earned or bought
questions.explanation: Peter's rebuke in Acts 8:20-21 emphasizes that God's gifts are not commodities to be purchased, teaching integrity in faith matters.

questions.question: According to Acts 8:21, why does Simon have 'neither part nor lot in this matter'?
options: Because he did not believe in Jesus
Because his heart was not right in God's sight
Because he was not from Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Because his heart was not right in God's sight
questions.explanation: Acts 8:21 explicitly states Simon's heart was not right before God, disqualifying him from sharing in the blessings.

questions.question: What does Peter urge Simon to do in order to be forgiven?
questions.correctAnswer: Repent and pray to God
questions.explanation: Acts 8:22 commands Simon to repent and pray to God so that his heart’s thoughts may be forgiven.

questions.question: What is the condition of Simon's soul as perceived by Peter, described in Acts 8:23?
options: In the gall of bitterness and bond of iniquity
questions.correctAnswer: In the gall of bitterness and bond of iniquity
questions.explanation: Acts 8:23 describes Simon's spiritual state as bitter and bound by sin, highlighting the need for repentance.

questions.question: What does Simon do after Peter's rebuke and call to repentance?
options: He asks Peter to pray for him
questions.correctAnswer: He asks Peter to pray for him
questions.explanation: Acts 8:24 states Simon asked them to pray to the Lord for him that none of the things spoken would happen to him.

questions.question: After dealing with Simon, what do Peter and John do next according to Acts 8:25?
options: They returned to Jerusalem and preached the gospel in many Samarian villages
They went to Samaria to baptize more believers
They stayed in Samaria to teach for months
They traveled to Ethiopia to preach
questions.correctAnswer: They returned to Jerusalem and preached the gospel in many Samarian villages
questions.explanation: Acts 8:25 records their return to Jerusalem and continued preaching in many Samaritan villages.

questions.question: What role does the angel of the Lord play in Philip’s mission according to Acts 8:26?
options: Instructs Philip to travel south toward Gaza
Tells Philip to return to Jerusalem
Encourages Philip to preach in Samaria
questions.correctAnswer: Instructs Philip to travel south toward Gaza
questions.explanation: Acts 8:26 shows the angel telling Philip to arise and go toward the way going down to Gaza.

questions.question: Why was the Ethiopian eunuch in Jerusalem according to Acts 8:27?
questions.correctAnswer: To worship
questions.explanation: Acts 8:27 says he had come to Jerusalem to worship.

questions.question: True or False: Simon believed in Jesus Christ, was baptized, and continued with Philip, marveling at the miracles done.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Acts 8:13 says Simon believed, was baptized, and followed Philip, amazed by the miracles.

questions.question: True or False: Peter told Simon that he could purchase the gift of God with money if he paid enough.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Acts 8:20 states Peter rebuked Simon, saying the gift of God cannot be purchased with money.

questions.question: True or False: The Ethiopian eunuch was reading the book of Psalms while sitting in his chariot.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Acts 8:28 says the eunuch was reading Esaias (Isaiah) the prophet, not Psalms.

hard.title: Acts Chapter 8 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Acts Chapter 8.

questions.question: What did Philip hear the eunuch reading from the prophet?
questions.correctAnswer: A passage from Isaiah
questions.explanation: Philip heard the eunuch reading from the prophet Esaias (Isaiah), as stated in Acts 8:30.

questions.question: What did the eunuch ask Philip regarding the scripture he was reading?
options: Of whom speaketh the prophet this?
questions.correctAnswer: Of whom speaketh the prophet this?
questions.explanation: The eunuch asked Philip, 'I pray thee, of whom speaketh the prophet this?' (Acts 8:34).

questions.question: What did Philip preach to the eunuch?
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus
questions.explanation: Philip preached unto him Jesus, beginning at the same scripture (Acts 8:35).

questions.question: What did the eunuch desire to do when they came to water?
questions.correctAnswer: Be baptized
questions.explanation: The eunuch asked, 'See, here is water; what doth hinder me to be baptized?' (Acts 8:36).

questions.question: What did Philip say was necessary for the eunuch to be baptized?
options: He must believe with all his heart
questions.correctAnswer: He must believe with all his heart
questions.explanation: Philip said, 'If thou believest with all thine heart, thou mayest' (Acts 8:37).

questions.question: What happened to Philip after he baptized the eunuch?
options: He was taken up by the Spirit of the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: He was taken up by the Spirit of the Lord
questions.explanation: After the baptism, 'the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip' (Acts 8:39).

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'baptizo' in Acts 8:38 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: To immerse
questions.explanation: 'Baptizo' means 'to immerse' in water, which is the act performed by Philip in the baptism of the eunuch.

questions.question: Which literary device is primarily used in Acts 8:32-33 when referring to the suffering servant?
questions.correctAnswer: Metaphor
questions.explanation: The description of being 'led as a sheep to the slaughter' is a metaphor for suffering and sacrifice, as found in Acts 8:32-33.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects with the theme of the eunuch's baptism in Acts 8:36?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 53:5
questions.explanation: Isaiah 53:5 speaks of healing and sacrifice, paralleling the eunuch's understanding of Jesus' suffering, which led to his desire for baptism in Acts 8:36.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage furthers the concept of belief before baptism found in Acts 8:37?
questions.correctAnswer: Mark 16:16
questions.explanation: Mark 16:16 states that 'He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved,' which aligns with the belief requirement in Acts 8:37.

questions.question: What comes before Philip’s encounter with the eunuch in Acts 8:26?
options: The apostles receiving the Holy Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: Philip preaching in Samaria
questions.explanation: Before Philip went to the eunuch, he was preaching in Samaria, as stated in Acts 8:5.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'great joy' in Acts 8:8 signify about the impact of Philip's preaching?
options: It indicates the success of his ministry
It reflects the joy of the apostles
questions.correctAnswer: It indicates the success of his ministry
questions.explanation: The phrase 'great joy' in Acts 8:8 signifies the positive impact and success of Philip's ministry in Samaria.

questions.question: The statement, 'Thy money perish with thee' in Acts 8:20 illustrates what principle?
questions.correctAnswer: The danger of greed
questions.explanation: Peter's statement about Simon's money illustrates the danger of greed and the idea that God's gifts cannot be bought, as seen in Acts 8:20.

questions.question: True or False: Philip was an apostle.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Philip was one of the seven deacons chosen in Acts 6:5, not one of the twelve apostles.

questions.question: True or False: The eunuch was a high-ranking official in Ethiopia.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The eunuch was of great authority under Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, as stated in Acts 8:27.

theological.title: Acts Chapter 8 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Acts Chapter 8 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 8:4 teach about salvation and mission?
options: Salvation naturally leads to active witness and preaching of the word.
Salvation is only for those in Jerusalem and the apostles.
Salvation is dependent on performing miracles to validate faith.
Salvation is a secret experience not to be shared publicly.
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation naturally leads to active witness and preaching of the word.
questions.explanation: Acts 8:4 shows that those scattered abroad went everywhere preaching the word, indicating that salvation necessarily results in active evangelism and mission.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 8:12 teach about the relationship between belief, baptism, and the kingdom of God?
options: Belief in the kingdom of God and Jesus Christ precedes baptism as the sign of entrance.
Baptism alone guarantees entrance to the kingdom of God without belief.
The kingdom of God is unrelated to baptism and belief.
Baptism nullifies the need for personal faith in Jesus Christ.
questions.correctAnswer: Belief in the kingdom of God and Jesus Christ precedes baptism as the sign of entrance.
questions.explanation: Acts 8:12 indicates people believed Philip's preaching concerning the kingdom of God and Jesus, and then were baptized, showing belief precedes baptism as a covenant sign.

questions.question: What doctrine about the Holy Spirit is taught in Acts 8:17?
options: The Holy Spirit is given through the laying on of apostles' hands after baptism.
The Holy Spirit is automatically given at baptism without further action.
The Holy Spirit cannot be given to Samaritans.
The Holy Spirit is given only through prophecy, not apostles' hands.
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy Spirit is given through the laying on of apostles' hands after baptism.
questions.explanation: Acts 8:17 records that Peter and John laid hands on the baptized Samaritans, and they received the Holy Ghost, teaching the normative means of Spirit reception here.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 8:22 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Longsuffering
questions.explanation: Peter commands Simon to repent and pray that his heart’s thought may be forgiven (Acts 8:22), demonstrating God's longsuffering, giving time for repentance despite wickedness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Acts 8:39?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Acts 8:39 shows the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, demonstrating God's sovereign control over events and mission.

questions.question: How does Acts 8 prepare for the universal mission of the church as seen in later epistles?
options: By showing the gospel extending beyond Jerusalem to Samaria and Ethiopia, fulfilling the command to be witnesses to all nations.
By limiting the gospel strictly to Jewish audiences.
By emphasizing only miraculous signs as proof of the gospel.
By focusing solely on the apostles’ authority in Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: By showing the gospel extending beyond Jerusalem to Samaria and Ethiopia, fulfilling the command to be witnesses to all nations.
questions.explanation: Acts 8 describes the scattering of believers leading to gospel expansion to Samaria and the Ethiopian eunuch, prefiguring the universal mission in the New Testament.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme is fulfilled in the baptism of the Ethiopian eunuch in Acts 8:36-38?
options: The inclusion of Gentiles and outsiders into the covenant people through faith and baptism.
The rejection of non-Jewish worshippers from salvation.
The exclusive salvation of the Jewish nation.
The necessity of Old Testament temple worship for salvation.
questions.correctAnswer: The inclusion of Gentiles and outsiders into the covenant people through faith and baptism.
questions.explanation: The Ethiopian eunuch represents a Gentile outsider included by faith and baptism, fulfilling promises of Gentile inclusion in God's covenant community.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 8:18 and Acts 8:20 teach about the gift of the Holy Spirit?
options: The gift of the Holy Spirit cannot be bought with money but is freely given by God.
The gift of the Holy Spirit can be earned by good works.
The gift of the Holy Spirit is only for apostles.
The gift of the Holy Spirit is given only after rigorous ritual.
questions.correctAnswer: The gift of the Holy Spirit cannot be bought with money but is freely given by God.
questions.explanation: Simon’s offer to buy the power (v18) is rebuked by Peter (v20), emphasizing the Spirit’s gift is not for sale but a divine grace.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about repentance and forgiveness is taught in Acts 8:21 and Acts 8:24?
options: True repentance is necessary for forgiveness and restoration to fellowship with God.
Repentance is irrelevant if one believes miracles.
Forgiveness depends on human effort alone.
questions.correctAnswer: True repentance is necessary for forgiveness and restoration to fellowship with God.
questions.explanation: Peter tells Simon to repent because his heart is not right (v21), and Simon asks for prayer to avoid judgment (v24), showing repentance’s role in forgiveness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about the authority of Scripture and the role of the Spirit in understanding is taught in Acts 8:29 and Acts 8:30?
options: The Spirit guides believers to understand Scripture through the gospel messenger.
Scripture can be understood without the Spirit or preaching.
The Spirit only inspires prophecy, not understanding of Scripture.
Believers must interpret Scripture independently of others.
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit guides believers to understand Scripture through the gospel messenger.
questions.explanation: The Spirit directs Philip to approach the eunuch (v29), and Philip asks if he understands what he reads (v30), showing Spirit-led interpretation through preaching.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Acts 8:14-17 shows that Samaritan believers were incomplete Christians because they lacked the Holy Ghost. What does the passage actually teach?
options: The passage teaches that receiving the Holy Ghost through apostolic laying on of hands is an essential part of full incorporation into the church.
The passage shows that Samaritans were fully saved without the Holy Ghost.
The passage teaches that baptism alone guarantees the Holy Ghost.
The passage indicates that the Holy Ghost is optional for believers.
questions.correctAnswer: The passage teaches that receiving the Holy Ghost through apostolic laying on of hands is an essential part of full incorporation into the church.
questions.explanation: Verses 14-17 show apostles sent Peter and John to pray for the Samaritans to receive the Holy Ghost by laying on hands, indicating the Spirit’s reception completes their inclusion.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 8:9-11 teach about human sin and false religion?
options: Human sin can manifest as deception through false signs and sorcery that mislead people away from God.
False religion is harmless and leads to salvation.
Sorcery and false claims are accepted means to demonstrate divine power.
Deception is not a serious problem in spiritual matters.
questions.correctAnswer: Human sin can manifest as deception through false signs and sorcery that mislead people away from God.
questions.explanation: Simon’s use of sorcery to bewitch people (vv9-11) illustrates how sin leads to false religion and deception opposed to the gospel.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Acts 8:26 by the angel of the Lord directing Philip?
questions.correctAnswer: Providence
questions.explanation: The angel directing Philip to the desert road (v26) shows God’s providential guidance in mission and salvation history.

questions.question: What doctrinal synthesis is taught by combining Acts 8:35 and Acts 8:37 about the nature of Christ and faith?
options: Faith in Jesus as the Son of God is essential for salvation and baptism.
Faith is irrelevant if one reads Scripture.
Belief in Jesus' humanity alone is sufficient for baptism.
Jesus’ divine sonship is a minor doctrine unrelated to faith.
questions.correctAnswer: Faith in Jesus as the Son of God is essential for salvation and baptism.
questions.explanation: Philip preaches Jesus (v35), and the eunuch confesses belief that Jesus is the Son of God before baptism (v37), showing faith in Christ’s divine identity is crucial.

questions.question: How does Acts 8:25 contribute to the narrative arc of the early church’s expansion?
options: It shows the gospel spreading from Samaria back to Jerusalem and into surrounding villages, continuing the missionary movement.
It indicates the church’s isolation in Jerusalem only.
It limits evangelism exclusively to Jewish populations.
It shows the apostles abandoning mission after persecution.
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the gospel spreading from Samaria back to Jerusalem and into surrounding villages, continuing the missionary movement.
questions.explanation: Acts 8:25 shows those who testified and preached in Samaria returned to Jerusalem and continued preaching in many Samaritan villages, illustrating gospel expansion.
